brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

finish.summary: A compact three-cell sewing caddy: three full hex bases bolted into a tight cluster, each with a different drop-in bin (3-compartment, 2-compartment, open), and all 12 open edges capped. check_build: no issues, mesh collision clear. 21 parts.

requirements.requirement: Sorted storage for small notions (pins, buttons, bobbins, needles)
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 gives three separate compartments in cell 0,0,0.

requirements.requirement: Separate spaces for medium items (thread spools, tape measure, chalk)
requirements.evidence: bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 gives two compartments in cell 0,1,0.

requirements.requirement: Open space for bulky items (scissors, fabric scraps, pincushion)
requirements.evidence: bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full is an open, undivided full-depth bin.
Joint bolts jointBolt:0#0,0#0, 0#0,0#5 and 0#0,1#1 join all three bases; the LOOSE_BODY warnings stopped once these were fitted.
12 caps close every open edge; check_build has no issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
